objective: Test newly inspected first-party Opus 5.5 documentation surfaces for a literal target-owner exhaustive useful-behavior specification (W1) or an implementation-level complete characterization (W2), without inferring global nonexistence from absence.

Uses the selective phrase 'The capabilities that matter most for prompting are' before describing capability areas.
A prompting-relevant subset is not an exhaustive useful-behavior specification.
Documents Claude app system prompts as interface behavior that can be periodically updated.
States Claude 4.6-generation and later model IDs are fixed snapshots, but this does not expose exact weights, full serving semantics, or a complete executable characterization.
Describes system cards as documenting capabilities, safety evaluations, and responsible deployment decisions.
No explicit exhaustive-all-useful-behavior attestation observed on the system-card index.
Uses 'Key use cases include' before capability/use-case examples.
Selective use-case language is affirmative evidence against treating the page as an exhaustive useful-behavior specification.
